title: Open at the Core: Moving from Proprietary Technology to Building a Product on Open Source Software
near_miss_reason: Only staggered element is Table 9 (AI open-source repositories; entry_date = first month a non-owner company commits, repo-specific, AI_repository_analysis.Rmd lines 103-131). The published regression is a within-repo cross-group triple difference: log(commits+1) ~ entrant*external*post | repo + month on repo x contributor-group (owner/entrant/external) x month cells, so the repo-level post indicator (on for the owner group too) is an additional staggered regressor next to entrant:post and external:post (two treatment interactions), with repo (not repo x group) FE plus group main effects. Same structure as near-miss mksc.2017.1043 (PROTOCOL 5b 'triple differences with an additional staggered regressor'). All repos in the sample eventually see entry (inner merge with treatment_dates), so only not-yet-treated repos serve as controls. Violation is extra treatment regressors, not time-varying controls, so not a 5c candidate.
eligible_reason: Headline analyses (Tables 2-8, Figures 2-7) have a single treated unit (Chromium repo, or the Edge browser) at common dates (Microsoft announcement Dec 2018; Edge release Jan 2020): feols(y ~ Chromium*Announcement*PostRelease) with no or repo/organization FE, clusters = 3-5 repos/browsers. Not staggered. Table 9 is staggered but its only reported specification is a DDD with an extra staggered post regressor (see near_miss_reason).
design_notes: R Markdown (Main.Rmd for browser analyses; Commits_categorization/AI_repository_analysis.Rmd for Figure 8 and Table 9). Browser analyses: daily/weekly/monthly series for Chromium vs Firefox/WebKit (commits, code changes, reviewers), browsers (vulnerability reporters, functionalities, release cycles, market shares by country). Lead-lag plots use i(period, Chromium) with period FE. Table 9: 13,740 AI repos from GHArchive, contributor groups by email domain (Crunchbase, university lists), balanced repo x group x month panel within +/-11 months of entry, separately for company-led and community repos; cluster repo.
main_or_robustness: main (browser case study); Table 9 is a main-text extension
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Table 9 entry months vary by repo (monthly, 13,740 repos), but the count was not computed: commits_AI_categorized.csv must first be generated by emails_categorization.ipynb (not run).

specs.exclusion_reason: triple difference with additional staggered regressor (repo-level post) and two treatment interactions (entrant:post, external:post); repo rather than repo x group FE
single treated unit (Chromium) at common dates; no unit/time FE
